title: Episode 000000
action_generation_prompt: The robot's left hand, on the left side of the view, grips the green cube between its thumb and fingers, lifts it, carries it toward the table center, sets it down and releases it. The robot's right hand then closes its fingers around the green cylinder, lifts it, carries it over the cube, lowers it onto the cube's top face and releases it, leaving the cylinder resting on top of the cube. Keep the camera fixed; preserve robot geometry, physically valid joint motion, and normal gripper opening and closing.
publisher_annotation: place the square building blocks in the center with left hand and put the cylindrical building blocks on top with right hand.

review.prompt_protocol_note: Applied by analogy: this episode is a dual-arm Airbot MMK2 with five-finger dexterous hands, not a Humanoid Everyday or NVIDIA GR1 video. The humanoid_action_v1 rules (robot-relative side, per-hand roles, coordination, actual end state, shared constraint sentence, complete single-task clip) were used as written.
review.selection_reason: Complete single-task clip retained: left hand moves the cube to the table center, then right hand stacks the cylinder on it. Both phases belong to one stacking task, so the full 176-frame sequence is kept without cropping or first_substep splitting.
review.usable_prompt: The robot's left hand, on the left side of the view, grips the green cube between its thumb and fingers, lifts it, carries it toward the table center, sets it down and releases it. The robot's right hand then closes its fingers around the green cylinder, lifts it, carries it over the cube, lowers it onto the cube's top face and releases it, leaving the cylinder resting on top of the cube. Keep the camera fixed; preserve robot geometry, physically valid joint motion, and normal gripper opening and closing.

chronology.observation: Initial frame: robot-left hand (image left) is open and raised at the left edge with its thumb extended below it; robot-right hand (image right) is open at the right edge, mostly out of view. Green cube lies left of centre, green cylinder (green top with blue/yellow/white stripes on its side, hole in top) lies right of centre. The left hand advances toward the cube and tilts down; the right hand stays at the right edge.

Left hand lowers with the thumb on the table side of the cube and the fingers/palm side above and behind it; the fingers and thumb close on the cube (contact visible from about frame 14, firmly pinched by frame 24-25). The cube is held between thumb and the fingers/palm, not merely pushed.

Left hand lifts the cube and carries it toward the right and forward, the cube tilting in the grip (frames 36-46) with its shadow separated from it, while the forearm extends into view. The right hand remains static at the right edge.
Left hand lowers the cube onto the table near the table centre and the thumb backs off; by frame 58-60 the cube sits flat on the table and the hand is no longer holding it.

Left hand withdraws toward the left edge and stops with fingers open (it stays idle there until the end except for a small drift at frames 168-174). Right hand begins moving inward toward the cylinder.

Right hand arrives over/beside the cylinder with its palm facing down and fingers extended, then lowers; by about frame 84-96 the fingers wrap the cylinder's sides and the thumb comes in underneath/beside it. The cylinder is partly hidden by the hand.
Right hand is nearly stationary with fingers curled around the cylinder, finishing the grasp (slow finger closure). The cylinder is still on the table, occluded.

Right hand lifts the cylinder off the table (visible raised and tilted in the fingers at about frames 126-134) and carries it left toward the cube, remaining in contact with the cylinder with fingers and thumb.
Right hand brings the cylinder over the cube and lowers it onto the cube's top face (cylinder over cube at frames 136-142, resting on the top face with fingers still around it by frames 146-154).
Fingers open and release; the thumb/lower fingers slide away. Cylinder stands upright on top of the cube with the hole facing up.

Right hand lifts and withdraws toward the upper right, ending partly out of frame. Cylinder remains upright on the cube; left hand still at the left edge, open. Final state: cylinder stacked on the cube near the table centre.

anatomical_side_evidence: Head camera looks forward over the table; the hand entering from the image-left edge is the robot's left hand and the one entering from the image-right edge is the right hand. This agrees with the other evidence below.

Parquet telemetry: eef_sim_pose_state holds two end-effector poses (columns 0-5 and 6-11). The first has y = +0.21 at frame 0, moving to about +0.02 during frames 0-60 (the left-hand cube transport phase), then returns to +0.22 and stays still; the second has y = -0.18 and begins moving only after frame 60 (right-hand phase). With x forward, positive y is robot-left and negative y is robot-right.

Wrist cameras: cam_left_wrist_rgb sees the green cube near the hand at frame 20, and cam_right_wrist_rgb sees the striped cylinder in the hand at frame 100. The front camera faces the robot, so its image is mirrored: the active hand at frame 20 is on the image-right there, matching robot-left.
The Parquet column names were not available for the poses, so the pose-column to side mapping rests on the y-sign convention and its agreement with the head-camera and wrist-camera views.

arm_roles.left: Acts first (frames about 14-60). Pinches the green cube between thumb and fingers/palm, lifts and carries it toward the table center, sets it down and releases it. Afterwards it is retracted at the left edge, open and idle; it does not touch the cylinder or the stack.
arm_roles.right: Idle at the right edge until about frame 60. Then approaches the green cylinder, wraps fingers and thumb around it (grasp complete by about frame 98-118), lifts and carries it over the cube, lowers it onto the cube's top face, opens to release it (frames 156-160) and withdraws upward and rightward.

review.coordination: Strictly sequential, no hand-to-hand transfer and no overlapping manipulation. The left hand finishes positioning the cube and has withdrawn (frame 60-70) before the right hand starts moving toward the cylinder; the right hand then stacks the cylinder onto the cube the left hand placed. The left hand provides no support during stacking.

observed_outcome.description: The green cube ends at the table centre, sitting flat on the table; the striped green cylinder rests upright on the top face of the cube, with both hands withdrawn (left at the left edge, right retreating out of view at upper right). Nothing dropped; no regrasp. The placement of the cylinder appears roughly centred on the cube top; the final frame shows it stable.

source_annotation.task_prompt: place the square building blocks in the center with left hand and put the cylindrical building blocks on top with right hand.
source_annotation.scene_annotation: On the left, there is a green building block. On the right, there is another green building block.

subtask_timeline.label: Grasp the green build blocks with the left gripper
Place the green build blocks on the center of the table with the left gripper
Grasp the green cylindrical build blocks with the right gripper
Place the green cylindrical build blocks on the green build blocks with the right gripper

source_annotation_discrepancies: Publisher text matches the visible task and sides (left hand: square block to the centre; right hand: cylinder on top).

Subtask timing differs: 'Grasp ... with the left gripper' covers frames 0-25, but the visible fingers close on the cube at roughly frames 14-25, with approach and hand pre-shaping from frame 0. 'Place ... on the center' (26-59) actually includes lifting and carrying the cube; release is at about frame 58-60.

'Grasp the green cylindrical build blocks with the right gripper' (60-118) mixes the right-hand approach (60-84) with a slow finger closure (84-118); the lift of the cylinder starts about frame 120-126, inside the publisher's 'Place' phase (119-155).
'End' (156-175) starts at the visible release (156-160); frames 162-175 are the right hand withdrawing.
Source subtask labels say 'gripper' while the hands are five-finger dexterous hands; the prompt uses hand wording.

The source scene text says 'another green building block' on the right; it is a striped green cylinder (its sides show blue, yellow and white bands), not a second cube. The publisher also calls the cube 'square building blocks' (plural); one cube and one cylinder are present.
uncertainties: Exact finger-level grasp of the cube by the left hand (which fingers press) is partially occluded; the cube is described as pinched between the thumb and the fingers/palm side.

Right-hand finger positions around the cylinder during frames 84-124 are occluded by the hand and the shadow; the lift moment is estimated at about frames 120-126 from the cylinder moving out of position.
Exact frame at which the cylinder stops touching the right-hand fingers on the cube is around 156-160 because of motion blur at 160-164.
Robot-relative left/right rests on head-view geometry, y-sign of the end-effector poses, and wrist-camera content, not on published pose column names.

inspection_coverage.initial_png_note: generation input/first_frame.png inspected at native 640x480 after the full sequence; it matches decoded frame 0.

title: Episode 000001
action_generation_prompt: The robot's left hand grasps the glasses case with its fingers over the top and thumb underneath, lifts it, and sets it across the tops of the red and green blocks, then releases and withdraws. Afterward the right hand reaches in, pinches the blue block between its thumb and fingers, lifts it, and sets it upright on the case's right end, then opens and moves clear while the left hand stays idle. Keep the camera fixed; preserve robot geometry, physically valid joint motion, and normal gripper opening and closing.
publisher_annotation: place the square building blocks in the center with left hand and put the cylindrical building blocks on top with right hand.

review.prompt_protocol_note: RoboCOIN Airbot MMK2 is a dual-arm robot with five-finger dexterous hands, not a Humanoid Everyday or NVIDIA GR1 dataset. humanoid_action_v1 is applied by analogy: robot-relative left/right hand, separate per-hand roles, coordination order, per-hand contact changes and the actual end state, with the shared constraint sentence appended verbatim.
review.selection_reason: Complete single-task clip retained: the left hand places the glasses case on the red and green blocks, then the right hand places the blue block on the case. These are ordinary phases of one stacking task, so the full video is kept without cropping or a first_substep.
review.usable_prompt: The robot's left hand grasps the glasses case with its fingers over the top and thumb underneath, lifts it, and sets it across the tops of the red and green blocks, then releases and withdraws. Afterward the right hand reaches in, pinches the blue block between its thumb and fingers, lifts it, and sets it upright on the case's right end, then opens and moves clear while the left hand stays idle. Keep the camera fixed; preserve robot geometry, physically valid joint motion, and normal gripper opening and closing.

chronology.observation: Initial state: glasses case rests on the table at image-left; red block and green block stand upright in the middle; blue pentagonal-prism block lies at image-right of them. Robot's left hand (image-left, open) is beside the case. The right hand is only partly visible at the right image edge. The left hand lowers and its thumb moves under the case's near edge while the fingers settle over the top.

Left hand closes onto the case: fingers over the top, thumb beneath/near edge. The case starts to slide and lift (case appears off the table and motion-blurred by frame 34-36). The right hand stays open and static at the right edge.
Left hand lifts the case and carries it toward the red and green blocks, raising the arm so the forearm and cable enter the view.

Case held by the left hand just above the red block and green block, bridging them; the hand adjusts height and orientation, lowering gradually (the case is still carried and the thumb still supports it near the red block at frames 66-68).

Case is lowered onto the tops of the red and green blocks (touching by about frame 72-73) and rests across both, spanning them lengthwise. The left thumb/fingers remain next to the case edge near the red block.
Left hand releases (fingers opening, native frame 85 shows the hand lifting away with the case staying put) and withdraws toward image-left; case stays stacked on the two blocks.
Left hand rests open at image-left, idle for the rest of the clip. The right hand moves in from the right edge toward the blue block, fingers extended, with the thumb opposed.
Right hand lowers onto the blue block and closes; by native frame 133 the block is held between the thumb and the other fingers beside the green block.
Right hand lifts the blue block clear of the table (frames 138-144) and raises it, carrying it up and left over the right end of the case (frame 146-152).

Right hand lowers the blue block to the case's upper surface near the right (green-block) end; the arm with its cabling is now visible. The block touches the case by about frame 164-168 and is oriented upright.
Right hand opens and lets go (frame 177: blue block stands upright on the case, thumb beside it and fingers raised); block stays in place.

Right hand slides back and out; its thumb and finger sweep past the blue block's right side (motion-blurred at frame 187, blue block still visible on the case, possibly very slightly shifted). The clip ends before the right hand fully clears. Left hand still idle.

anatomical_side_evidence.conclusion: The hand at image-left is the robot's left hand and the hand entering from image-right is the robot's right hand. Image left matches robot left in the head view.
evidence: Telemetry (observation.state, joint names from metadata): left_arm joints 1-6 and left_hand joints 1-12 change substantially in frames 0-110, the period when the image-left hand grasps, lifts and places the case, while right_arm joints are essentially unchanged until about frame 75 and move mainly in frames 75-188 when the image-right hand picks and places the blue block.
cam_left_wrist_rgb at frame 50 shows the case-like pale grey-purple object beside the hand and cam_right_wrist_rgb at frame 140 shows the blue block between the fingers, matching the head-view hands.
cam_front_rgb views the scene from the far side, with the hand carrying the case early and the blue-block hand late, consistent with the head view's role assignment.

Publisher instruction assigns the first task (square blocks/case) to the left hand and the second (cylindrical block on top) to the right hand, which agrees with the visible sequence. The publisher text was not used as the sole evidence.

arm_roles.left: Robot's left hand (image-left): the only hand active in frames 0-96. It grasps the glasses case with fingers over the top and thumb underneath, lifts it, carries it over the red and green blocks, lowers it so it spans both, releases and withdraws. It stays open and idle afterwards, so it neither supports nor stabilizes the stack during the right-hand placement.
arm_roles.right: Robot's right hand (image-right): stationary and partly out of view in frames 0-96. From about frame 97 it approaches the blue block, pinches it between thumb and fingers (about frames 126-134), lifts and carries it above the case's right end, lowers it onto the case top, opens, and withdraws (frames 171-187).

review.coordination: Strictly sequential, no hand-to-hand transfer or simultaneous manipulation: left hand finishes and withdraws first (about frame 96), then the right hand performs its pick and place while the left hand stays idle at the left. The left hand's placement forms the support (case on two blocks) that the right hand's block is placed onto.

observed_outcome.description: The glasses case is bridged across the tops of the red and green blocks. The blue block ends standing upright on the right end of the case's top surface after the right hand opens (frame 177). During the right hand's final withdrawal (frames 180-187) its thumb and finger sweep past the block, which still appears on the case with perhaps a very slight shift in the last blurred frame. The right hand has not completely cleared the case at the clip end.

subtasks: Grasp the glasses case with the left gripper

source_annotation.scene_annotation: The green block is in the center, The red block is in the front-left, The blue block is in the front-right, The yellow block is not present, The purple block is not present, The glasses case is in the front-left
source_annotation.use: Used only as an annotation starting point; chronology comes from the decoded frames.

source_annotation_discrepancies: The publisher instruction says 'square building blocks in the center' placed by the left hand; visibly the left hand places a rounded glasses case (not a building block) across a red block and a green block, with a rectangular cuboid shape for each. The subtask label names the case ('Grasp the glasses case with the left gripper').

The instruction says 'cylindrical building blocks' on top by the right hand; the visible block is a blue pentagonal (five-sided) prism, not a true cylinder, and it is placed upright near the right end of the case, not at the center.
Subtask labels call the end effectors 'grippers', but the robot has five-finger dexterous hands.

Subtask timeline: Grasp case 0-28, place case 29-73, grasp blue block 74-130, place blue block 131-174, End 175-187. Visually, the left hand's grasp closes about frames 24-36 and the case is lowered onto the blocks by about 72, so the 'place case' label spans the lift and carry as well. The release/withdrawal at 79-96 is labeled as 'grasp blue block' although the right hand only begins to approach the block at about 97 and closes about 126-134. The blue block lifts from about 138 and touches the case about 164-168, with release about 171-177; the 'End' label begins at 175 while the right hand is still releasing and withdrawing until 187.
uncertainties: Exact finger contact points on the case and the blue block are partly occluded in the head view; 'fingers over the top and thumb underneath' for the case is the visible configuration at native frames 31-37, while the case may also be supported by the palm side.
Whether the blue block is slightly displaced by the right hand's thumb sweep in the final blurred frames (180-187) cannot be resolved; it appears to stay on the case.
The head view shows the case relative to the red and green blocks from above at an oblique angle; the case clearly spans both blocks by frame 85 but exact overlap is approximate.
The right hand's position at the very end is not fully clear of the case.

title: Episode 000002
action_generation_prompt: The robot's left hand closes its fingers and thumb around the green cube, lifts it, carries it toward the table center, sets it down and opens, then withdraws. The right hand then pinches the small green cylinder from the right side, carries it to the cube, holds it on top of the cube, releases it so it rests on the cube's top face, and withdraws. Keep the camera fixed; preserve robot geometry, physically valid joint motion, and normal gripper opening and closing.
publisher_annotation: place the square building blocks in the center with left hand and put the cylindrical building blocks on top with right hand.

review.prompt_protocol_note: Applied by analogy. This is a dual-arm Airbot MMK2 with five-finger dexterous hands from RoboCOIN, not a Humanoid Everyday or NVIDIA GR1 video; the humanoid_action_v1 rules (robot-relative side, per-hand roles, coordination, actual end state, complete single-task clip) were used.
review.selection_reason: Complete single-task clip retained: left hand places the cube, then right hand stacks the cylinder on it. These are ordered phases of one stacking task, so the full sequence is kept without cropping, shortening or a first_substep branch.
review.usable_prompt: The robot's left hand closes its fingers and thumb around the green cube, lifts it, carries it toward the table center, sets it down and opens, then withdraws. The right hand then pinches the small green cylinder from the right side, carries it to the cube, holds it on top of the cube, releases it so it rests on the cube's top face, and withdraws. Keep the camera fixed; preserve robot geometry, physically valid joint motion, and normal gripper opening and closing.

chronology.observation: The robot-left hand enters from the image-left edge with fingers extended; its thumb tip rests against the green cube's left face (frames 0-12) while the palm approaches. By frames 16-33 the palm and curled fingers come down over the cube's top and its thumb slides underneath on the near side, closing around it. The right hand is stationary at the image-right edge with open fingers, beside the small multicolored cylinder (green top face, striped side), which sits flat on the table. Left-arm telemetry joints change; left-hand joint mean rises from 0.22 at frame 20 to 0.65 by frame 40.

The left hand holds the cube between curled fingers and thumb and lifts it off the table (frame 48 native shows the cube raised with its shadow separated from it) while moving it rightward and away from the robot.

The left hand carries the cube, still held, across the table toward the scene center, with only small repositioning (left-arm joint changes continue until about frame 80 and then reverse). The cube is lowered toward the table, with the thumb pad beneath it and fingers over the top (frames 84-90).

The left hand opens its fingers and releases the cube onto the table near the image center (roughly x 280-350, y 200-300 of 640x480). The cube stays upright and in place. Publisher label for the placement ends at frame 94.

The left hand pulls back toward the image-left edge and stays open and still for the rest of the clip; the thumb tip remains visible at the left edge, with no further contact with the cube. The right hand begins moving (right-arm telemetry change from about frame 90-100) and advances from the right edge, fingers around the cylinder. By frame 126-144 the right hand curls around the cylinder with the thumb and fingers on its sides, still on or just above the table.

The right hand grasps and lifts the cylinder off the table (frame 148 native shows the cylinder gripped between the thumb and fingers at the hand's right) and carries it leftward, bringing it from the right edge toward the cube. The right-hand joint mean rises from about 0.42 to 0.67-0.73 as the hand closes.

The right hand positions the cylinder directly above the cube's top face (native frames 168 and 200 show the cylinder hovering over the cube with the thumb and fingers at its sides) and lowers it until it touches the top. It then holds the cylinder on the cube for a long dwell with almost no visible change (about frames 190-255), likely fine placing/alignment. The cube does not move or topple. The left hand stays open at the image-left edge and does not touch the objects.

The right-hand fingers release the cylinder; by frames 258-264 the cylinder is resting on the cube top, with the right hand's thumb and fingers opened and moving away to the upper-left (frame 262 native).

The right hand withdraws up and rightward out of the object area, finally into the upper-right corner with fingers extended (frames 274-282); the left hand is open at the left edge. The cylinder remains stacked, upright and centered on top of the cube at the scene center, and nothing falls.

anatomical_side_evidence.conclusion: The hand entering from the image-left edge is the robot's left hand, and the one from the image-right edge is the robot's right hand.
evidence: Parquet telemetry (observation.state layout from info.yaml: left_arm joints 1-6, right_arm joints 1-6, left_hand 12, right_hand 12): left-arm joints change by about 1.6 rad over frames 0-40, while right-arm joints change by only about 0.03; the right arm becomes active from about frame 90, as the image-right hand begins moving. Left-hand joint mean rises at frames 20-60 (the cube grasp) and the right-hand joint mean rises at frames 120-260 (the cylinder grasp).

The cam_left_wrist_rgb view at frame 60 shows the green cube pressed against the hand during the first phase, and cam_right_wrist_rgb at frame 200 shows the striped cylinder in its fingers during the stacking phase.
The head camera looks away from the robot's body along the table, so image-left corresponds to the robot's left, consistent with the telemetry.
anatomical_side_evidence.caveat: The cam_front_rgb view is a different perspective; it was only used as a side check.

arm_roles.left_hand: Active first. Closes its thumb and fingers around the green cube, lifts it, carries it toward the table center and releases it onto the table (frames 0-100), then stays open and still at the left edge without touching any object.
arm_roles.right_hand: Passive and stationary at the right edge until about frame 100, then active. It grasps the small green cylinder between its thumb and fingers, lifts it, carries it to the cube, holds it above the cube's top face and then on it, and releases it (frames 100-264), then withdraws to the upper-right.

review.coordination: Sequential, not simultaneous. The left hand completes its pick-and-place of the cube and withdraws before the right hand starts to move; the right hand then stacks the cylinder on the placed cube. There is no hand-to-hand transfer and no stabilizing hold by the left hand during stacking; the cube sits on the table unsupported while the cylinder is placed.

observed_outcome.description: The green cube rests upright on the table near the scene center and the small green cylinder with striped sides sits upright and centered on top of the cube. Both hands are away from the objects. Nothing was dropped and there were no retries or regrasps.

source_annotation.scene_annotation: The green block is in the front-left, The red block is not visible, The blue block is not visible, The yellow block is not visible, The purple block is not visible, The glasses case is not visible

source_annotation_discrepancies: The publisher instruction says 'square building blocks' and 'cylindrical building blocks' in the plural, but the video shows one cube and one small cylinder.

The instruction says the cube is placed 'in the center'. The cube ends near the middle of the table surface in the head view, but its position is only moderately central, closer to the left-center of the frame at about x 300 of 640, and it is moved only a short distance from its start at the image-left.

The scene annotation says the green block is in the front-left and other blocks are not visible. The visible cylinder has a green top face with colored (yellow/blue/green) bands, which the scene annotation does not mention.

The subtask label for grasping the cube ends at frame 33 and placement runs frames 34-94. Visually, the grasp closes at about frames 24-36 and the cube is lifted from about frame 36-48, and its release occurs at about frames 90-96, which matches closely.

The label 'Grasp the green cylindrical build blocks' spans frames 95-136, but the right hand only reaches the cylinder at about frames 120-146 and the lift occurs at about frame 146, so the label is a bit early. The 'Place' label spans 137-264, which includes the carry (146-168) and a long hold on top (about 190-255); the actual release is at about 256-264.
The publisher 'End' label starts at frame 265, after release, which matches.
uncertainties: Whether the cube is fully lifted or partially slid across the table in frames 36-90 cannot be fully established; frame 48 suggests it is raised, and the shadow is separate from the cube.
The exact contact points of the left-hand fingers on the cube are hidden behind the palm; the thumb sits under the near face and the other fingers curl over the top.
The long hold of the cylinder on the cube (about frames 190-255) may include slow alignment and release; the exact frame at which the fingers lose contact is estimated at 256-260.
Cylinder appearance: green top face with a striped yellow/blue/green side; the identity is described by appearance only.
The robot-relative side rests on telemetry names and wrist cameras together with the head-camera view; it was not cross-checked with a body view because no camera shows the robot's torso.
